Redo.dc.html.title: 2 · The redo so far · now called Visits, with Who visits your website and What people looked at · press Play to switch By and Compare with

todayBoxes.text:
The four boxes

• New and returning add up to more than everyone. 93.6% plus 20.9% is 114.5%.
• That's because someone who came for the first time and then came back in October is in both.
• New visitors and Returning visitors aren't compared with September.

todayLine.text:
New and returning visitors a day

• A dot marks a day with a conversion. More Handles has them every day.
• So every day has a dot, and the dots all look the same. They tell you nothing.

todaySquares.text:
Where each kind of visitor lands

• One group has two numbers. New is 24,115 visits here and 24,289 in the table.
• Some squares have more conversions than visits. Returning visitors on Unclassified pages made 2,033 visits and 3,552 conversions.
• That's because it counts every conversion, not each visit that converted.
• On Interests it says there are no conversions. The table shows some.

todayTable.text:
The table

• Returning visitors show 11,809 conversions from 9,510 visits. It says "124.2% of visits".
• Unknown has 1,540 people, 4.3% engaged and no conversions. They may be robots, or people who said no to cookies.
• On Age, Google doesn't know the age for about 3 in 4 visits. Unknown is the biggest row.
• Interests has 123 of Google's long names. The top one is "Travel Buffs". One person can have many.

redoTop.text:
The redo so far

• The page now counts visits, as you asked on 3 November.
• It's called Visits now, in its title and in the menu.
• The squares are gone. Who visits your website takes their place.
• What people looked at is new. It sits under the daily line, at your comment.
• The table is as it is today, faults and all. Board 1 lists them.

redoVisits.text:
Now in visits

• The boxes count visits. New and returning no longer add up to more than everyone.
• Every box says how it compares with September, by name.
• The line shows new and returning visits a day, not people.
• Compare with lays September over October as dashed grey lines. Press Play to try it. Added at your comment on 3 November.
• September sits under October by date, so the weekends don't line up.
• The dots are gone, because the chart with menus doesn't draw them. Open question 5 in the plan asks if you want them back.
• The line under the title says visits too.

redoWho.text:
New. Who visits your website, by …

This is the chart you approved on a page's own screen on 3 November. Not built here yet.

• Use By to switch between New or returning, Age, Gender, Browser, Operating system and Interest. Press Play to try it.
• The orange bars are October. The grey bars are September.
• Each bar is visits, with its number on it.
• Age and Gender leave out visits Google can't place. The line under the title says how many it knows.
• Interest shows the 8 biggest of 123, with short names.

redoTreemap.text:
New. What people looked at, by kind of page

The treemap from the kit. It counts every page people looked at, not just the first. Changed at your comment on 3 November.

• Each box is one of your page groups, sized by views. That's 152,926 views of 9,538 pages in October.
• It uses views because one visit can see many pages of the same kind. Adding up visits would count that visit again for each page.
• Not sorted yet is the biggest, at nearly 1 in 3 views. That's 3,198 pages with no group yet.
• Blog, Electrical and Lighting are too small to name. You only see their figures on hover.

redoLimits.text:
Limits

• Google's counts differ a little. The boxes say 35,739 visits. New, returning and not known add up to 35,923.
• Device isn't in By. The device menu at the top already does that.
• In this drawing, Compare with on the bars doesn't switch. It always shows September.

redoAsk.text:
Still to decide

The chart has its own By menu. The table under it has its own switch. Today they can show different things.

Should one choice change both?
